knowledge_graph.title: Pelizaeus–Merzbacher disease
knowledge_graph.description: Pelizaeus–Merzbacher disease is an X-linked neurological disorder that damages oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system. It is caused by mutations in proteolipid protein 1, a major myelin protein.

text_blocks.snippet: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease (PMD) is a rare, inherited neurological disorder that primarily affects the brain and spinal cord, specifically the myelin sheath that insulates nerve fibers. It's a type of leukodystrophy, meaning it's characterized by the abnormal development or destruction of myelin. PMD is caused by mutations in the PLP1 gene, which is crucial for producing a protein essential for myelin formation.
snippet_highlighted_words: a rare, inherited neurological disorder that primarily affects the brain and spinal cord, specifically the myelin sheath that insulates nerve fibers

list.snippet: Progressive Deterioration: PMD is a progressive disease, meaning symptoms worsen over time.
